# Vendored crates

Third-party crates that this fork modifies live here until a GitHub fork exists for each of them (DECISIONS.md D10, D31). Every crate under `vendor/<name>` is listed in the workspace `[workspace] exclude` array (not `members`) and is wired in through a path `[patch]` entry in the workspace `Cargo.toml`, so it is a standalone package: `cargo -p <name>` does not target it, `cargo test --workspace` does not run its tests, and it is checked with `cargo test --manifest-path vendor/<name>/Cargo.toml`. Each section below records the upstream revision the copy was taken from, the exact patch entry, and the local changes, so the copy can later be replaced by the intended git-patch form (`[patch."<upstream url>"] <name> = { git = "<fork url>", rev = "<sha>" }`) once the fork repository exists. Later lanes append sections; nobody rewrites this file.

## yawc

- Upstream: https://github.com/zed-industries/yawc
- Revision: 71a452f551cac178367eaac5d7418a09afa1f3a2 (version 0.3.3; copied from the cargo git checkout of that revision, minus `.git`)
- Patch entry: `[patch."https://github.com/zed-industries/yawc"] yawc = { path = "vendor/yawc" }` (the dependency line `yawc = { git = "https://github.com/zed-industries/yawc", rev = "71a452f551cac178367eaac5d7418a09afa1f3a2", version = "0.3.3" }` is unchanged; `vendor/yawc/Cargo.toml` keeps `version = "0.3.3"` so it satisfies it). Intended git-patch form once a fork exists: `[patch."https://github.com/zed-industries/yawc"] yawc = { git = "<fork url>", rev = "<sha>" }`.
- Local changes:
  - `src/wasm.rs`: the body of `WebSocket::connect` after `web_sys::WebSocket::new` is factored into a private `from_stream`, and a new `pub async fn connect_with_protocols(url: Url, protocols: &[&str]) -> Result<Self>` constructs the browser socket with `web_sys::WebSocket::new_with_str_sequence` so subprotocols (`Sec-WebSocket-Protocol`) can be offered from the browser, where request headers cannot be set. Used by `crates/remote`'s WebSocket transport to carry the session token as the second subprotocol.
  - `src/wasm.rs`: `impl Drop for WebSocket` calls `web_sys::WebSocket::close()`. The event closures are `forget()`-ed, so without this the browser socket stayed open after the Rust value was dropped.
  - `src/wasm.rs`: `from_stream` holds the still-connecting `web_sys::WebSocket` in a `PendingSocket` guard whose `Drop` calls `close()`, so a `connect*` future dropped before `onopen` (a dial raced against a timeout) closes the pending browser socket instead of leaking it.
  - `src/wasm.rs`: a wasm `Options { max_payload_read, max_read_buffer }` (builder methods named like the native ones) and `WebSocket::connect_with_protocols_and_options(url, protocols, options)`. The message handler checks the incoming message's `byte_length()`/`length()` against `max_payload_read` before copying it out of the browser and closes with 1009 when exceeded; it tracks the bytes queued for the consumer (`queued_bytes`, decremented in `poll_next`) and closes with 1008 when a message would push the queue past `max_read_buffer`. Defaults are unlimited, so `connect`/`connect_with_protocols` behave as before.
  - Native code is untouched. An upstream PR with the same diff is intended for `zed-industries/yawc`.

- Local changes (all of them are `vendor/alacritty_terminal.patch`, a diff against the pristine copy so the rebase job can re-vendor a new rev and `patch -p1 < vendor/alacritty_terminal.patch` inside `vendor/alacritty_terminal`; no rustfmt run, no other source line touched):

## sqlite-wasm-rs (not vendored; provenance record)

- Upstream: crates.io `sqlite-wasm-rs` 0.5.5 = https://github.com/Spxg/sqlite-wasm-rs (used as `libsqlite3-sys = { package = "sqlite-wasm-rs", version = "0.5.5" }` in `crates/sqlez/Cargo.toml`'s wasm table; the native build keeps `libsqlite3-sys` 0.30.1)
- Revision: the crates.io package, pinned by `Cargo.lock` checksum `dc3efc0d…` (not a `vendor/` copy: it is unmodified and reached through the registry, so it has no `[patch]` entry and is not in `[workspace] exclude`)
- Bundled SQLite: 3.53.0 (`sqlite3/sqlite3.h:149`), compiled by the crate's `build.rs` from its own `sqlite3/sqlite3.c` with `cc` against a vendored musl shim; no network access. Provenance verified on 2026-09-03: `sqlite3.c` and `sqlite3.h` in the 0.5.5 package are byte-identical to the files in `https://sqlite.org/2026/sqlite-amalgamation-3530000.zip` (`sqlite3.c` SHA-256 `c94657c2a08ed5f3f61a25f0018eb2f64ec42fd053da26d741db9e52e6ffaa77`, SHA3-256 `bb317fbbd2b3bc53233ddd5894bf4d2dc6f533445f350d4235dbcc86f65af4ec`; `sqlite3.h` SHA-256 `8e43a79982422f4720685f62839718f0e41410c1b71355aa32af3615ccd9e31d`, both from the crate and from the zip). Re-run the comparison whenever the crate version changes (release checklist).
- Compile flags (`build.rs` `FULL_FEATURED`): `SQLITE_OS_OTHER`, `SQLITE_USE_URI`, `SQLITE_THREADSAFE=0`, `SQLITE_TEMP_STORE=2`, `SQLITE_OMIT_DEPRECATED`, `SQLITE_OMIT_LOAD_EXTENSION`, `SQLITE_OMIT_SHARED_CACHE`, `SQLITE_ENABLE_API_ARMOR`, plus the extensions `BYTECODE_VTAB`, `DBPAGE_VTAB`, `DBSTAT_VTAB`, `FTS5`, `MATH_FUNCTIONS`, `OFFSET_SQL_FUNC`, `PREUPDATE_HOOK`, `RTREE`, `SESSION`, `STMTVTAB`, `UNKNOWN_SQL_FUNCTION`, `COLUMN_METADATA`. Zed uses none of the extensions; the client-state image is untrusted input, so `sqlez::Connection::open_scratch_from_image` rejects any schema object other than tables and indexes (virtual tables included), sets `SQLITE_DBCONFIG_DEFENSIVE`/`trusted_schema=OFF` on the scratch and on the connection that receives the restore, requires `PRAGMA quick_check`, caps the image at `MAX_IMAGE_BYTES` and interrupts the migration dry-run after a step budget. Building the amalgamation ourselves without those extensions (through a `links = "wsqlite3"` override, b6 §7 item 1) is the follow-up that removes the extension code from the bundle altogether.
- Version skew: the native database is SQLite 3.46.0 (`libsqlite3-sys` 0.30.1) and the browser's is 3.53.0. Images are plain database files and are portable between the two (`db::AppDatabase::new_with_image` natively, `open_with_image` in the browser); nothing in the schema depends on a post-3.46 feature.

Intended git-patch form once a fork exists: `[patch."https://github.com/zed-industries/wasm_thread"] wasm_thread = { git = "<a fork of zed-industries/wasm_thread>", rev = "<one commit on top of 0cf96c7 with the changes below>" }`.
- Why: the editor route ships `script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'` (BUILD-SPEC 7.6, b7 §3.30) and the pinned revision calls `js_sys::eval` five times (`src/wasm32/utils.rs:15, 26, 34`, `src/wasm32/mod.rs:60, 300`), which that CSP blocks; `'unsafe-eval'` on the route was the recorded fallback until this copy landed (b9 `ZS_CSP_UNSAFE_EVAL`).
- Local changes:
  - `src/wasm32/utils.rs`: `available_parallelism` and `is_web_worker_thread` read `js_sys::global()` instead of `js_sys::eval("self")`; `get_wasm_bindgen_shim_script_path` first reads `globalThis.__zsBindgenShimUrl` (`SHIM_URL_GLOBAL`, set by the loader before `start`, CONTRACTS.md §8.4) and only then falls back to the stack-trace heuristic, now built from `js_sys::Error::new("").stack` and a `js_sys::RegExp` (the same expression as the removed `js/script_path.js`) instead of `eval`. `Builder::wasm_bindgen_shim_url` keeps precedence over both.
  - `src/wasm32/mod.rs`: `WorkerMessage::post` uses `js_sys::global()`; `spawn_for_context` no longer evals `js/module_workers_polyfill.min.js` before `options.set_type(WorkerType::Module)` (module workers are native in every browser with cross-origin-isolated shared memory: Chrome 80, Safari 15, Firefox 114).
  - `src/wasm32/js/script_path.js` and `src/wasm32/js/module_workers_polyfill.min.js` deleted (no longer included); `web_worker_module.js` and `web_worker.js` are untouched, and the worker entry stays a `blob:` module URL (`worker-src 'self' blob:`).
- Verification: `script/check-wasm -p gpui_web` and `-p zed_web` reach the copy through the patch (`-p wasm_thread` is not a member); `script/build-web` fails closed when `grep -rn 'js_sys::eval' vendor/wasm_thread/src` is not empty or the built `zed_web_bg.wasm` still carries the removed scripts. Rebase job: when upstream Zed bumps the `rev` on the two dependency lines, re-vendor from the new rev, re-apply the changes above, update the revision here and run `script/check-wasm -p gpui_web`. See docs/briefs/b7-edge-gates-entry.md 3.33.

## pet-fs

- Upstream: https://github.com/microsoft/python-environment-tools (crate `crates/pet-fs`)
- Revision: bb8e04607b96a3865d6aa4bb2a5a5a82ce05b5f0 (version 0.1.0; the rev on the seven `pet*` lines in Cargo.toml, copied from the cargo git checkout of that revision: `crates/pet-fs/{Cargo.toml, src/}` plus the checkout root's `LICENSE` (MIT); nothing else from the checkout)
- Patch entry: `[patch."https://github.com/microsoft/python-environment-tools.git"] pet-fs = { path = "vendor/pet-fs" }` (the dependency lines are unchanged; only `pet-fs` is replaced; every other `pet*` crate (the six on the dependency lines and the in-repo crates they pull in, `pet-core`, `pet-python-utils`, `pet-uv`, ...) keeps coming from the git checkout, and their in-repo `pet-fs = { path = "../pet-fs" }` dependencies resolve to this copy (`cargo tree -i pet-fs` lists them); `vendor/pet-fs/Cargo.toml` keeps `version = "0.1.0"`, which must stay equal to the workspace version at that rev or cargo reports the patch as unused). Intended git-patch form once a fork exists: `[patch."https://github.com/microsoft/python-environment-tools.git"] pet-fs = { git = "<a fork of microsoft/python-environment-tools>", rev = "<one commit on top of bb8e0460 with the path.rs change below>" }`.
- Local changes:
  - `src/path.rs`: the three non-test `#[cfg(unix)]` gates become `#[cfg(any(unix, target_family = "wasm"))]`: the `use std::path::MAIN_SEPARATOR;` import, the Unix block of `strip_trailing_separator` and the Unix early `return` of `norm_case`. Upstream's bodies are entirely `#[cfg(windows)]`/`#[cfg(unix)]`, so on wasm32-unknown-unknown (neither) both functions compiled to `()` against a `-> PathBuf` signature (E0308). The browser build follows the Unix rules: `/`-separated paths (D11 home is `/home/web`) and `norm_case` as a no-op. Native code is untouched (the `unix` arm is the same gate, so Unix and Windows compile byte-for-byte the same source). A two-line comment above each function-body gate explains the wasm arm. The `#[cfg(unix)]` tests are left as they are (they do not run on wasm).
  - `Cargo.toml` standalone-manifest lines, because the copy sits outside python-environment-tools' workspace and outside ours: `version.workspace = true` → `version = "0.1.0"`, `edition.workspace = true` → `edition = "2021"`, `license.workspace = true` → `license = "MIT"` (the values at the checkout's root `Cargo.toml` `[workspace.package]`). Not part of the upstream PR.
  - `Cargo.lock`: not in the upstream checkout; written by the standalone `cargo test --manifest-path vendor/pet-fs/Cargo.toml` run (the crate has no dev-dependencies, so it resolves only `glob` and `log`) and kept so that run is reproducible. Not part of the upstream PR.
- Verification: `cargo check -p pet-fs` (native) and `script/check-wasm -p pet-fs` both target the copy through the patch; `cargo test --manifest-path vendor/pet-fs/Cargo.toml` runs its unit tests. Rebase job: when upstream Zed bumps the `rev` on the `pet*` lines, re-vendor `crates/pet-fs` from the new rev, re-apply the three-gate change, update the revision here and run both checks. An upstream PR with the `src/path.rs` diff is intended for microsoft/python-environment-tools; when merged and the rev bumped, delete the patch table and this directory.

## tree-sitter-python

- Upstream: crates.io tree-sitter-python 0.25.0 = https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter-python
- Revision: 293fdc02038ee2bf0e2e206711b69c90ac0d413f (tag v0.25.0, see `.cargo_vcs_info.json`; copied from the registry package directory minus `.cargo-ok` and `Cargo.toml.orig`; `Cargo.lock` is the registry package's lock, kept so the standalone test run resolves offline)
- Patch entry: `[patch.crates-io] tree-sitter-python = { path = "vendor/tree-sitter-python" }` (the dependency line `tree-sitter-python = "0.25"` is unchanged; the copy keeps `version = "0.25.0"` so it satisfies it). Intended git-patch form once a fork exists: `[patch.crates-io] tree-sitter-python = { git = "<a fork of tree-sitter/tree-sitter-python>", rev = "<one commit on top of 293fdc02 with the build.rs hunk below>" }`.
- Why: `src/scanner.c` includes `<stdio.h>` (directly, and through `src/tree_sitter/array.h` → `alloc.h`); wasi-sdk 25's `stdio.h` reaches `__seek.h` → `wasi/api.h`, which `#error`s under `--target=wasm32-unknown-unknown` (not a WASI platform), so cc-rs fails inside the build script. The tree-sitter runtime at the workspace's git rev (`43623ec`) ships a wasm32 libc header subset in the `tree-sitter-language` crate (`crates/language/wasm/include`: `assert.h`, `ctype.h`, `endian.h`, `inttypes.h`, `stdint.h`, `stdio.h`, `stdlib.h`, `string.h`, `wchar.h`, `wctype.h`), publishes its path to dependents as `DEP_TREE_SITTER_LANGUAGE_WASM_HEADERS` (`links = "tree-sitter-language"`, `cargo::metadata=wasm-headers=…` in its build script), and its CLI template `crates/cli/src/templates/build.rs` adds that directory to the grammar's include path on `wasm32-unknown-unknown`; 0.25.0's bindings were generated before that template change.
- Local changes:
  - `bindings/rust/build.rs`: the template's block, verbatim, inserted after the msvc `-utf-8` flag: when `TARGET == "wasm32-unknown-unknown"`, read `DEP_TREE_SITTER_LANGUAGE_WASM_HEADERS` (panic with the template's message when unset) and `c_config.include(&wasm_headers)`. cc-rs `-I` directories rank above `script/wasm-cc`'s `-isystem` sysroot, so `<stdio.h>`, `<stdlib.h>`, `<string.h>`, `<assert.h>` and `<stdint.h>` resolve to the tree-sitter shim (`<stdbool.h>` is clang's own). Nothing else changes: `src/`, `queries/`, `bindings/rust/lib.rs` and the registry-normalised `Cargo.toml` are byte-identical to the 0.25.0 package, and the block runs only for that target, so native builds compile exactly the same objects with the same flags.
  - Known noise, left as upstream has it: on wasm the shim's `assert.h` `__assert_fail` trips cc-rs's default `-Wextra` (`-Wunused-parameter`, four `cargo:warning` lines); those are C-compiler warnings relayed by the build script, not rustc warnings, so `-D warnings` does not see them. The fix belongs in tree-sitter's header, not in the grammar.
- Upstream PR: the same one-hunk diff against tree-sitter/tree-sitter-python (regenerating the bindings with a tree-sitter CLI that carries the template block produces it); when released, bump `tree-sitter-python = "0.25"` past it, delete the patch line and the `exclude` entry, delete this directory.
- Verification: `script/check-wasm -p tree-sitter-python` (a non-member `-p`, resolved through the patch) and `cargo check -p tree-sitter-python` natively; `languages` (`load-grammars`) is the member that reaches it in the browser closure.

The libc symbols `scanner.c` links against (`calloc`, `free`, `iswalpha`, `iswdigit`, `iswspace`) are in the runtime's `lib/src/wasm-stdlib/imports.txt` subset, which `tree-sitter`'s `lib.c` compiles in under `TREE_SITTER_WASM_STDLIB` for this target.
- Tests: `cargo test --manifest-path vendor/tree-sitter-rust/Cargo.toml` (`test_can_load_grammar`; the dev-dependency `tree-sitter = "0.25"` resolves from crates.io, outside this workspace's `[patch]` tables). From the workspace: `cargo check -p tree-sitter-rust` natively and `script/check-wasm -p tree-sitter-rust`.
- Upstream: no separate PR; a tree-sitter-rust release regenerated with a tree-sitter CLI at or after 43623ec carries this block. When one ships, bump the `tree-sitter-rust` line, delete the patch line and this directory.

## tree-sitter-cpp

- Upstream: https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter-cpp
- Revision: 5cb9b693cfd7bfacab1d9ff4acac1a4150700609 (version 0.23.4; the rev on the `tree-sitter-cpp` line in Cargo.toml, copied from the cargo git checkout of that revision: the files the manifest's `include` list packages (`Cargo.toml`, `LICENSE`, `bindings/rust/{build.rs, lib.rs}`, `grammar.js`, `queries/*.scm`, `src/{grammar.json, node-types.json, parser.c, scanner.c}`, `src/tree_sitter/*.h`, `tree-sitter.json`) plus `README.md` (named by `readme`) and the repository's `Cargo.lock`, kept so the standalone test run resolves the same dependency versions; nothing else from the checkout (no node/python/swift/go bindings, `test/`, `examples/` or CI files))
- Patch entry: `[patch."https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter-cpp"] tree-sitter-cpp = { path = "vendor/tree-sitter-cpp" }` (the dependency line `tree-sitter-cpp = { git = "https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter-cpp", rev = "5cb9b693cfd7bfacab1d9ff4acac1a4150700609" }` is unchanged; a git dependency carries no version requirement, so the vendored `0.23.4` satisfies it). Intended git-patch form once a fork exists: `[patch."https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter-cpp"] tree-sitter-cpp = { git = "<a fork of tree-sitter/tree-sitter-cpp>", rev = "<one commit on top of 5cb9b693 with the build.rs change below>" }`.
- Why: `src/scanner.c` includes `src/tree_sitter/alloc.h`, whose `#include <stdio.h>` resolves to wasi-sdk 25's `stdio.h` → `__seek.h` → `wasi/api.h`, which `#error`s under `--target=wasm32-unknown-unknown` (not a WASI platform), so cc-rs fails inside the build script — the same failure as tree-sitter-python and tree-sitter-rust above; 0.23.4's `bindings/rust/build.rs` predates the tree-sitter CLI template's wasm32-unknown-unknown block. Two further gaps are specific to this scanner: it declares `wchar_t` (`Scanner::delimiter`) and uses C11 `static_assert`, which hosted libcs provide through `<stdlib.h>` and `<assert.h>`, but the `tree-sitter-language` crate's freestanding header set (tree-sitter 43623ec `crates/language/wasm/include`) declares `wchar_t` only in its `wchar.h` and has no `static_assert` in its `assert.h`.
- Local changes:
  - `bindings/rust/build.rs`: the wasm32-unknown-unknown block of the tree-sitter CLI's `build.rs` template (tree-sitter 43623ec `crates/cli/src/templates/build.rs:10-16`), verbatim, inserted after the msvc `-utf-8` flag: when `TARGET == "wasm32-unknown-unknown"`, read `DEP_TREE_SITTER_LANGUAGE_WASM_HEADERS` (panic with the template's message when unset) and `c_config.include(&wasm_headers)`; cc-rs `-I` directories rank above `script/wasm-cc`'s `-isystem` sysroot, so `<stdio.h>`, `<stdlib.h>`, `<string.h>`, `<assert.h>`, `<wctype.h>` and `<stdint.h>` resolve to the tree-sitter shim (`<stdbool.h>` is clang's own). Inside the same target-gated block, two Zed Codespaces lines the template does not have, with a comment above them: `c_config.flag("-include").flag("wchar.h")` (pre-includes the shim's `wchar.h`, found through that `-I`, so `wchar_t` is declared for `scanner.c` and, harmlessly, `parser.c`) and `c_config.define("static_assert", "_Static_assert")` (spells the C11 keyword out). Native targets never enter the block, so they see the same `cc::Build` as before.
  - Nothing else changes: `src/`, `queries/`, `bindings/rust/lib.rs`, `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, `grammar.js`, `tree-sitter.json`, `LICENSE` and `README.md` are byte-identical to the checkout (`diff -r ~/.cargo/git/checkouts/tree-sitter-cpp-*/5cb9b69 vendor/tree-sitter-cpp` reports only `build.rs` and files the copy leaves out), so native builds compile exactly the same objects with the same flags.
  - Link-time note for the browser bundle (b7): the libc symbols `scanner.c` links against (`memcpy`, `memset`, `iswspace`, and `malloc`/`calloc`/`realloc`/`free` through `ts_*`) are in the runtime's `lib/src/wasm-stdlib/imports.txt` subset, which `tree-sitter`'s `lib.c` compiles in under `TREE_SITTER_WASM_STDLIB` for this target; `assert` expands to the shim's `static inline __assert_fail` (`__builtin_trap`) and `static_assert` is compile-time, so the scanner needs no other import.
  - Known noise, left as upstream has it: on wasm the shim's `assert.h` `__assert_fail` trips cc-rs's default `-Wextra` (`-Wunused-parameter`, four `cargo:warning` lines); C-compiler warnings relayed by the build script, not rustc warnings, so `-D warnings` does not see them.
- Upstream: the template block arrives in tree-sitter-cpp on its own with the next `tree-sitter init --update` there; the `wchar_t`/`static_assert` gap belongs in tree-sitter's freestanding headers (`crates/language/wasm/include/stdlib.h` declaring `wchar_t`, `assert.h` defining `static_assert`), after which the two extra lines can go. When both have shipped, bump the `tree-sitter-cpp` rev, delete the patch table, the `exclude` entry and this directory.
- Verification: `cargo check -p tree-sitter-cpp` natively and `script/check-wasm -p tree-sitter-cpp` (a non-member `-p`, resolved through the patch) from the workspace; `cargo test --manifest-path vendor/tree-sitter-cpp/Cargo.toml` standalone (`test_can_load_grammar` plus the lib.rs doc-test; the dev-dependency `tree-sitter = "0.24"` resolves from crates.io, outside this workspace's `[patch]` tables). `languages` (`load-grammars`) is the member that reaches it in the browser closure.

## tree-sitter-bash

- Upstream: crates.io tree-sitter-bash 0.25.1 = https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter-bash
- Revision: a06c2e4415e9bc0346c6b86d401879ffb44058f7 (the commit the crates.io package was published from, `.cargo_vcs_info.json`; copied from the registry package directory minus `.cargo-ok` and `Cargo.toml.orig`; `Cargo.lock` is the registry package's lock, kept so the standalone test run resolves offline)
- Patch entry: `[patch.crates-io] tree-sitter-bash = { path = "vendor/tree-sitter-bash" }` (the dependency line `tree-sitter-bash = "0.25.1"` is unchanged; the copy keeps `version = "0.25.1"` so it satisfies it, and a rebase that bumps that line past 0.25.1 makes cargo report the patch as unused). Intended git-patch form once a fork exists: `[patch.crates-io] tree-sitter-bash = { git = "<a fork of tree-sitter/tree-sitter-bash>", rev = "<one commit on top of a06c2e44 with the build.rs change below>" }`.
- Why: as for tree-sitter-python, `src/scanner.c` reaches `<stdio.h>` through `src/tree_sitter/array.h` → `alloc.h`, and wasi-sdk 25's `stdio.h` → `__seek.h` → `wasi/api.h` `#error`s under `--target=wasm32-unknown-unknown`, so cc-rs fails inside the build script. On top of that, the scanner calls `isdigit` at two sites (`scanner.c:1158`, `:1172`; every other character test in the file is the `isw*` family), and the header subset that fixes the first problem has no `isdigit`: the tree-sitter-language crate's `crates/language/wasm/include/ctype.h` declares only `isblank`/`isprint`, and the runtime's `lib/src/wasm-stdlib/imports.txt` (what `tree-sitter`'s `lib.c` compiles in under `TREE_SITTER_WASM_STDLIB`) carries no `isdigit` either, because wasi-libc's own `<ctype.h>` makes `isdigit` an inline macro that never becomes an import (the CLI's `.wasm` grammar route, `--target=wasm32-unknown-wasi -nostdlib`, never sees the subset headers). Under clang 19 with `-std=c11` the undeclared call is a hard error (`call to undeclared library function 'isdigit'`).
- Local changes (`bindings/rust/build.rs` only; `src/`, `queries/`, `bindings/rust/lib.rs`, `grammar.js`, `tree-sitter.json`, `LICENSE`, `README.md`, `Cargo.lock` and the registry-normalised `Cargo.toml` are byte-identical to the 0.25.1 package, so native targets compile exactly the registry sources with exactly the registry flags):
  - the tree-sitter CLI template's wasm32-unknown-unknown block (tree-sitter 43623ec `crates/cli/src/templates/build.rs:10-16`), verbatim, inserted after the msvc `-utf-8` flag: when `TARGET == "wasm32-unknown-unknown"`, read `DEP_TREE_SITTER_LANGUAGE_WASM_HEADERS` (panic with the template's message when unset) and `c_config.include(&wasm_headers)`. cc-rs `-I` directories rank above `script/wasm-cc`'s `-isystem` sysroot, so `<stdio.h>`, `<stdlib.h>`, `<string.h>`, `<assert.h>`, `<ctype.h>`, `<wctype.h>` and `<stdint.h>` resolve to the tree-sitter subset. Identical to the tree-sitter-python hunk.
  - inside that same block, one extra line with a comment: `c_config.define("isdigit", "iswdigit")` (`-Disdigit=iswdigit`, this target only). `iswdigit` is declared in the subset's `<wctype.h>` (scanner.c already includes it), is in `imports.txt` (`lib/src/wasm-stdlib/libc/ctype/iswdigit.c`: `(unsigned)wc - '0' < 10`), and returns the same answer as `isdigit` for every `int32_t` code point `lexer->lookahead` holds (`isdigit` on a value above 255 is undefined behaviour in C, so it is also the safer call; the scanner already passes `lookahead` to `iswalpha`/`iswalnum`/`iswdigit`/`iswspace` everywhere else). Kept in `build.rs` rather than as a `#if` in `scanner.c` so the C sources stay pristine and native objects (including `__LINE__` in the `array.h` assertion messages and `-g` line tables) are unchanged. If a later tree-sitter revision adds an `isdigit` declaration to the subset's `ctype.h`, the define rewrites that declaration too and clang reports conflicting types against `<wctype.h>`'s `iswdigit`; the rebase then simply drops this line.
  - The other libc symbols the scanner links against (`calloc`, `free`, `memcpy`, `memset`, `strcmp`, `iswalnum`, `iswalpha`, `iswdigit`, `iswspace`) are all in `imports.txt`; `assert` expands to the subset's static inline `__assert_fail`, which trips cc-rs's default `-Wextra` (`-Wunused-parameter`, four `cargo:warning` lines on wasm, the same noise tree-sitter-python records; C-compiler warnings relayed by the build script, not rustc warnings, so `-D warnings` does not see them).
- Upstream PR: two candidates, either of which retires the define: (a) tree-sitter/tree-sitter-bash replacing the two `isdigit(lexer->lookahead)` calls with `iswdigit` like the rest of the scanner (the template block then comes for free from a release regenerated with a tree-sitter CLI at or after 43623ec); or (b) tree-sitter/tree-sitter adding `isdigit` (musl's inline form) to `crates/language/wasm/include/ctype.h`. When a tree-sitter-bash release carries both the regenerated `build.rs` and an `isdigit`-free scanner, bump the `tree-sitter-bash` line, delete the patch line and the `exclude` entry, delete this directory.
- Verification: `script/check-wasm -p tree-sitter-bash` (a non-member `-p`, resolved through the patch) and `cargo check -p tree-sitter-bash` natively; `cargo test --manifest-path vendor/tree-sitter-bash/Cargo.toml` runs the crate's `test_can_load_grammar` (its dev-dependency `tree-sitter = "0.25"` resolves from crates.io, outside this workspace's `[patch]` tables). `languages` (`load-grammars`), `editor` and `grammars` are the members that reach it in the browser closure.

## async-tar

- Upstream: https://github.com/zed-industries/async-tar
- Revision: bd3ad6f89df9a9da7a8535958756d6bf465936a0 (version 0.6.1; the rev on the `async-tar` line in Cargo.toml, copied from the cargo git checkout of that revision: `Cargo.toml`, `src/`, `tests/` (with `tests/archives`), `LICENSE-APACHE`, `LICENSE-MIT`, `README.md`; `examples/`, `.github/`, `.gitignore`, `.rustfmt.toml` and `.cargo-ok` are not carried)
- Patch entry: `[patch."https://github.com/zed-industries/async-tar"] async-tar = { path = "vendor/async-tar" }` (the dependency line `async-tar = { git = "https://github.com/zed-industries/async-tar", rev = "bd3ad6f89df9a9da7a8535958756d6bf465936a0" }` is unchanged; a git dependency carries no version requirement, so the vendored `0.6.1` satisfies it). Intended git-patch form once a fork exists: `[patch."https://github.com/zed-industries/async-tar"] async-tar = { git = "<a fork of zed-industries/async-tar>", rev = "<one commit on top of bd3ad6f8 with the changes below>" }`.
- Why: `async-std` 1.13 compiles its `fs` module (and the filesystem methods of `async_std::path::Path`) only on `not(target_os = "unknown")`, so on wasm32-unknown-unknown the crate failed with 21 errors (`async_std::fs` unresolved in `archive.rs`, `builder.rs`, `entry.rs`, `header.rs`, `lib.rs`; the cascading `Sized`/`E0599` errors; and `Builder`'s `Drop`, because `async_std::task::block_on` on wasm spawns a `'static` local task instead of blocking). `dap`, `node_runtime` and `languages` keep the crate in the browser closure.
- Local changes (all gates are `#[cfg(not(target_family = "wasm"))]` stacked under the existing `#[cfg(feature = "runtime-…")]` lines; native code paths are byte-for-byte unchanged):
  - `src/lib.rs`: the `fs_canonicalize`, `symlink_metadata` and `metadata` helpers (both runtimes) are gated; a crate-doc paragraph lists what is unavailable on wasm.
  - `src/archive.rs`: the `fs` and `StreamExt` imports, the `TarError`/`fs_canonicalize`/`symlink_metadata` imports and `Archive::unpack` are gated (they are the only users). `Archive`, `ArchiveBuilder`, `Entries`, `RawEntries` and the header/pax parsing compile unchanged.
  - `src/builder.rs`: the `fs`, `Metadata`, `tokio_stream::StreamExt`, `metadata`, `other` and `symlink_metadata` imports, `Builder::{append_path, append_path_with_name, append_file, append_dir, append_dir_all}`, the free functions `append_path_with_name`, `append_file`, `append_dir`, `prepare_header_link`, `append_fs`, `append_dir_all`, and the `runtime-async-std` `impl Drop` (which calls `block_on`) are gated. `Builder::{new, mode, follow_symlinks, get_ref, get_mut, into_inner, append, append_data, finish}` stay. The `mode` and `follow` fields get `#[cfg_attr(target_family = "wasm", allow(dead_code))]` because only the gated methods read them; the struct doc says that on wasm an unfinished builder that is dropped writes no termination blocks.
  - `src/entry.rs`: the `fs`, `OpenOptions`, `Error`, `ErrorKind`, `SeekFrom`, `Component`, `PathBuf`, `filetime`, `TarError`, `fs_canonicalize`, `other` and `symlink_metadata` imports, `Unpacked::File(fs::File)`, `Entry::{unpack, unpack_in}` and `EntryFields::{path_lossy, unpack_in, unpack_dir, unpack, ensure_dir_created, validate_inside_dst}` are gated. Reading an entry (`AsyncRead`, `path`, `link_name`, `pax_extensions`, `header`) is unchanged. The `runtime-async-std` `Permissions` import is now `#[cfg(all(unix, feature = "runtime-async-std"))]`, mirroring the existing `runtime-tokio` line: only the unix arm of `_set_perms` names it, so as a path crate (compiled uncapped under CI's `-D warnings`) the old unconditional import would have been an `unused_imports` error on Windows.
  - `src/header.rs`: the `Metadata` imports, `Header::{set_metadata, set_metadata_in_mode}` and `fill_from` are gated. The `#[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")] fill_platform_from` arm (an `unimplemented!()` that referenced a `fs::Metadata` only imported on Windows, so it never compiled with `async-std` anyway) is removed together with the two Windows-only `use async_std::fs;`/`use tokio::fs;` lines that existed only for it (both unused on Windows, another latent `-D warnings` failure). The unix and windows `fill_platform_from` arms are untouched. In the pre-existing `cfg(any(windows, target_arch = "wasm32"))` `path2bytes` the return type is spelled `Cow<'_, [u8]>` (rustc 1.97's `mismatched_lifetime_syntaxes` warning; the unix arm already uses `'_`) and the wasm32 `bytes2path` loses two redundant braces (`unused_braces`); both are syntax-only fixes that the uncapped wasm build needs under `-D warnings`.
  - `Cargo.toml`: `filetime` moved from `[dependencies]` to a `[target.'cfg(not(target_family = "wasm"))'.dependencies]` table (only the gated code uses it). No other dependency line changed, so Cargo.lock only drops the git `source` of the `async-tar` entry.
- On wasm the crate exposes the archive reader (`Archive`, `ArchiveBuilder`, `Entries`, `Entry` as an `AsyncRead`, `Header`, `PaxExtensions`) and the in-memory writer (`Builder::append`/`append_data`/`finish`/`into_inner`); everything that touches local files does not exist there, so a caller that unpacks to disk (`crates/dap/src/adapters.rs`, `crates/node_runtime/src/node_runtime.rs`, `crates/languages/src/json.rs` call `Archive::unpack`) needs its own `cfg(not(target_family = "wasm"))` gate.
- Tests: `cargo test --manifest-path vendor/async-tar/Cargo.toml` runs the crate's own suite (`tests/all.rs`, `tests/entry.rs`, `tests/header`, the `pax` unit tests) natively (55 + 12 + 2 tests and 10 doc-tests at bd3ad6f8); `cargo check --manifest-path vendor/async-tar/Cargo.toml --no-default-features --features runtime-tokio` covers the tokio half of the gates; `script/check-wasm -p async-tar` is the wasm check. The standalone runs write `vendor/async-tar/Cargo.lock` (kept, like `vendor/lsp-types/Cargo.lock`, so they resolve offline; not part of the upstream PR) and a gitignored `vendor/async-tar/target/`. Rebase job: when upstream Zed bumps the `rev` on the `async-tar` line, re-vendor from the new rev, re-apply the changes above, update the revision here and run both.
- Upstream PR: the same diff (minus the `Permissions`/Windows-import cleanups, which are only needed because path crates compile uncapped) against zed-industries/async-tar; when merged, delete the patch table, bump the Cargo.toml rev, delete this directory.

An upstream PR with the `src/` diff is intended for microsoft/python-environment-tools (with matching wasm gates in `crates/pet-python-utils` (`find_executable`) and `crates/pet-core` (`impl Environment for EnvironmentApi`), which retire the `find.rs` shim and `WasmEnvironmentApi`); when merged and the rev bumped, delete the patch line, the `exclude` entry and this directory.

## tree-sitter-md

- Upstream: https://github.com/zed-industries/tree-sitter-markdown (Zed's fork of https://github.com/tree-sitter-grammars/tree-sitter-markdown, "fork of 9a23c1a with serialize() buffer-overflow fix")
- Revision: b596e737286780d7bfa9fcddceaeeb754574b352 (version 0.3.2; the rev on the `tree-sitter-md` line in Cargo.toml, copied from the cargo git checkout of that revision: the files the manifest's `include` list packages that exist there (`Cargo.toml`, `bindings/rust/{benchmark.rs, build.rs, lib.rs, parser.rs}`, `tree-sitter-markdown/{grammar.js, queries/*, src/*}`, `tree-sitter-markdown-inline/{grammar.js, queries/*, src/*}`, `common/html_entities.json`; the listed `common/grammar.js` does not exist upstream, whose file is `common/common.js`) plus `LICENSE` and `README.md`. Not carried: the node/python/swift/go bindings, `test/`, `Makefile`s, `package.json`, `contrib/`, `scripts/`)
- Patch entry: `[patch."https://github.com/zed-industries/tree-sitter-markdown"] tree-sitter-md = { path = "vendor/tree-sitter-md" }` (the dependency line `tree-sitter-md = { git = "https://github.com/zed-industries/tree-sitter-markdown", rev = "b596e737286780d7bfa9fcddceaeeb754574b352" }` is unchanged; a git dependency carries no version requirement, so the vendored `0.3.2` satisfies it). Intended git-patch form once a fork exists: `[patch."https://github.com/zed-industries/tree-sitter-markdown"] tree-sitter-md = { git = "<fork url>", rev = "<sha>" }`.
- Why: both scanners (`tree-sitter-markdown/src/scanner.c`, `tree-sitter-markdown-inline/src/scanner.c`) use `assert`; b596e737's `bindings/rust/build.rs` predates the tree-sitter CLI template's wasm32-unknown-unknown block, so on that target `<assert.h>` resolves to wasi-sdk 25's header and `assert` calls wasi-libc's `__assert_fail`, which nothing in the browser closure defines: `cargo check` passes (no link), but `script/build-web` fails at the `zed_web` link with `rust-lld: error: libtree_sitter_md-*.rlib(*-scanner.o): undefined symbol: __assert_fail` (twice, once per scanner). The other vendored grammars (tree-sitter-python, -rust, -cpp, -bash, -yaml above) get the tree-sitter-language crate's freestanding `assert.h`, whose `assert` expands to a `static inline __assert_fail` (`__builtin_trap`), through the same block.
- Local changes:
  - `bindings/rust/build.rs`: the wasm32-unknown-unknown block of the tree-sitter CLI's `build.rs` template (tree-sitter 43623ec `crates/cli/src/templates/build.rs:10-16`), verbatim, inserted after the msvc `-utf-8` flag: when `TARGET == "wasm32-unknown-unknown"`, read `DEP_TREE_SITTER_LANGUAGE_WASM_HEADERS` (panic with the template's message when unset) and `c_config.include(&wasm_headers)`; cc-rs `-I` directories rank above `script/wasm-cc`'s `-isystem` sysroot, so `<assert.h>`, `<stdio.h>`, `<stdlib.h>`, `<string.h>`, `<wctype.h>` and `<stdint.h>` resolve to the tree-sitter shim for all four C files (`<stdbool.h>` is clang's own). The crate already depends on `tree-sitter-language` (0.1, patched to the 43623ec checkout by `[patch.crates-io]`), which is what publishes that variable.
  - inside that same block, one extra line with a comment, as in tree-sitter-bash above: `c_config.define("isdigit", "iswdigit")` (`-Disdigit=iswdigit`, this target only). `tree-sitter-markdown/src/scanner.c:748` calls `isdigit(lexer->lookahead)`, and the subset's `<ctype.h>` declares only `isblank`/`isprint` (clang: "call to undeclared library function 'isdigit'"); `iswdigit` is declared in the subset's `<wctype.h>` (which that scanner includes), is in `imports.txt`, and answers the same for every code point. The inline scanner uses no `is*` function.
  - Nothing else changes: every other copied file is byte-identical to the checkout (`diff -rq ~/.cargo/git/checkouts/tree-sitter-markdown-*/b596e73 vendor/tree-sitter-md` reports only `build.rs` and files the copy leaves out), and the block runs only for that target, so native builds compile exactly the same objects with the same flags.
  - Known noise, left as upstream has it: on wasm the shim's `assert.h` `__assert_fail` trips cc-rs's default `-Wextra` (`-Wunused-parameter`, `cargo:warning` lines from the build script); C-compiler warnings relayed by the build script, not rustc warnings, so `-D warnings` does not see them.
- Upstream: the template block arrives on its own with the next `tree-sitter init --update` (or a `tree-sitter generate` with a CLI at or after 43623ec) in zed-industries/tree-sitter-markdown; when a rev carrying it is on the dependency line, delete the patch table, the `exclude` entry, the `tree-sitter-md` line in `script/check-wasm` and this directory.
- Verification: `cargo check -p tree-sitter-md` natively and `script/check-wasm -p tree-sitter-md` (a non-member `-p`, resolved through the patch; listed in `check-wasm`'s default set) from the workspace, then `script/build-web` links `zed_web` without the two `__assert_fail` errors. No standalone `cargo test --manifest-path` run: the crate's dev-dependency `tree-sitter = "0.23"` does not match the workspace's tree-sitter checkout, exactly as upstream has it. `grammars` (`load-grammars`) and `languages` are the members that reach it.

## parking_lot_core

- Upstream: https://crates.io/crates/parking_lot_core version 0.9.12 (the registry crate; `src/`, `build.rs`, `Cargo.toml` and the licences copied, the registry's `.cargo_vcs_info.json`, `.cargo-ok`, `Cargo.lock` and `Cargo.toml.orig` left out).
- Patch entry: `[patch.crates-io] parking_lot_core = { path = "vendor/parking_lot_core" }`; the workspace pins `parking_lot_core = "0.9.12"` so `gpui_web` can call the new function.
- Why: `src/thread_parker/wasm_atomic.rs` (the parker used with `nightly` + shared-memory wasm, which `gpui_web`'s `parking_lot` feature selects) parks with `memory.atomic.wait32`. Browsers forbid that instruction on the main thread and throw `RuntimeError: Atomics.wait cannot be called in this context` through the wasm frames, skipping every destructor; a contended mutex on the main thread (seen in `Worktree::remote` against a background worker during boot) therefore leaked gpui's `App` borrow and every later `cx.update` panicked "RefCell already borrowed".
- Local changes:
  - `src/thread_parker/wasm_atomic.rs`: a `CANNOT_WAIT` thread-local, `pub fn mark_current_thread_cannot_wait()`, and a spin-loop branch at the top of `park` and `park_until` for a marked thread. Unmarked threads (the workers) behave exactly as upstream.
  - `src/thread_parker/mod.rs` and `src/lib.rs`: re-export the function under the same `nightly` + wasm + atomics cfg as the parker itself.
  - `Cargo.toml` additionally declares the off-by-default `wasm-test-hooks` feature. With that feature, the wasm parker counts entries into the marked thread's untimed spin path and exports `main_thread_park_count` through the same two modules, so the browser regression can prove contention without a timing-based sleep. Native behavior is unchanged, and production bundles omit this instrumentation.
- Caller: `gpui_web::dispatcher::WebDispatcher::new` marks the main thread before any worker is spawned.
- Verification: `script/check-wasm` (the patched parker compiles under the workspace's wasm flags) and a native `cargo check -p project` (resolves through the patch, unchanged code); the browser takeover loop in `apps/web/.zs-dev/netdiag.mjs` no longer shows the exception.

## futures-util

The same browser-only parker now covers `lock::Mutex`'s internal waiter list;
the asynchronous lock API and native poisoning behavior are unchanged.

- Upstream: crates.io `futures-util` 0.3.32, futures-rs revision `d9bba94c239daa1175a5bb2958f37a5c72db3f6a` (`.cargo_vcs_info.json`), registry checksum `389ca41296e6190b48053de0321d02a77f32f8a5d2461dd38762c0593805c6d6`. The cached package is copied with licenses and provenance; `.cargo-ok` and its registry workspace lockfile are omitted. `Cargo.lock` is generated by the standalone checks and retained for their reproducibility.
- Patch entry: `[patch.crates-io] futures-util = { path = "vendor/futures-util" }`; excluded from workspace membership. No dependency version upgrade.
- Local changes: `Shared`'s waker mutex and the async mutex's waiter list on `wasm32-unknown-unknown` with `std` use `parking_lot::Mutex`, including registration, completion, notification and clone-drop lock sites. Its optional browser-only dependency is enabled by `std`, so native `std::sync::Mutex` (including poisoning) and no-std `spin::Mutex` retain upstream behavior. The existing D42-marked main-thread parker spins under contention; worker parking is unchanged. This fixes the real terminal environment `Shared<Task<_>>` contention path, which WebKit misleadingly reports as an out-of-bounds memory trap for a forbidden main-thread `memory.atomic.wait32`.
- Regression checks: standalone `cargo test --manifest-path vendor/futures-util/Cargo.toml --lib` covers registered-clone removal, notification, completion caching and native poisoning. The browser contention probe forces a worker to hold this exact notifier lock while the main thread polls another clone, with the test-only D42 counter as its release barrier; actual run results are recorded in round-4 status, not inferred from the test's presence.
- Rebase: re-copy the newly locked futures-util version, retain this target-only mutex patch and its tests, then validate native and no-std checks plus the browser contention regression. Upstreaming or switching the path patch to a fork requires separate publishing approval.

Astro follows the same build adaptation: `tree-sitter-astro-next` 0.1.1 from crates.io
(archive SHA-256 `794a4a59fc2d88e49b4bc41fef9522d77184a36f4e68bbaf545cd1eb2364c46e`).
Only `build.rs` adds the WASM headers; grammar/scanner/bindings are unchanged. Its
license and the original `virchau13/tree-sitter-astro` MIT notice are retained.
Astro configs/queries come from `zed-extensions/astro` revision
`03b07a4451df6f9dee6897afc06d841131dc8c05`, with its Apache-2.0 license beside them.

- Dockerfile: MIT-licensed grammar/scanner sources from `camdencheek/tree-sitter-dockerfile` revision `868e44ce378deb68aac902a9db68ff82d2299dd0`. The small Rust binding uses `tree-sitter-language::LanguageFn` instead of the upstream binding's older tree-sitter ABI; the parser itself is unchanged. The Dockerfile highlight queries carry the separate MIT license from `zed-extensions/dockerfile` revision `812fbe0e227d06e2c9e17864cd96985b064125ef` beside them in `crates/grammars/src/dockerfile`.
- HTML: the crates.io `tree-sitter-html` 0.23.2 package, with its MIT license from upstream revision `5a5ca8551a179998360b4a4ca2c0f366a35acc03`. Only `bindings/rust/build.rs` is patched.
- Both build scripts include `DEP_TREE_SITTER_LANGUAGE_WASM_HEADERS` on `wasm32-unknown-unknown`, so scanners use tree-sitter's freestanding character functions rather than unresolved WASI imports. Native compilation is unchanged. Both are optional dependencies of the `web-languages` feature; ordinary desktop builds do not enable them.
- Verification: `cargo test -p grammars --features web-languages` checks parsing and highlight/injection query compilation. `script/check-wasm -p zed_web --features zed_web/test-hooks` checks the browser closure; the linked bundle and browser tests remain separate checks. Rebase by updating the pinned source, retaining only bindings/build-script adaptations still required, and rerunning these checks.
